topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
consensus_response: V-band (57-66 GHz) is preferred in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) due to its smaller beamwidth, reducing interference between adjacent satellites. In Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), V-band's capacity decreases due to increased terrestrial interference and reduced spacing effects. Geostationary Orbit (GEO) configurations prefer Ka-band for high-capacity applications. The trade-off between frequency reuse and array factor size is critical in determining the optimal frequency band for inter-satellite communication in MEO and GEO configurations.
reference_context: Optical links may outperform RF solutions in LEO with 8 orbits or more, but V-band's capacity decreases due to increased interference in MEO. Ka-band is preferred in GEO for high-capacity applications.
